concepts.name: BIDMAS
concepts.definition: BIDMAS is an acronym for the order of operations in arithmetic: Brackets, Indices, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction.

concepts.name: Factorising into a Single Bracket
concepts.definition: Factorising into a single bracket is rewriting an algebraic expression as the product of a common factor and a simplified expression within parentheses.

concepts.name: Linear Equations
concepts.definition: A linear equation is a mathematical statement of equality between two expressions that forms a straight line when graphed.

concepts.name: Substitution into Formula
concepts.definition: Substitution into formula is the process of replacing variables in an algebraic expression with given numerical values to compute a result.

concepts.name: Writing Expressions
concepts.definition: Writing Expressions: The ability to translate a real-world scenario or verbal description into a correct mathematical algebraic statement.

concepts.name: Types, Naming and Estimating
concepts.definition: Types, naming, and estimating refer to classifying geometric figures, assigning correct mathematical labels, and approximating measurements without precise tools.

concepts.name: Area of Simple Shapes
concepts.definition: The measure of the two-dimensional space enclosed within the boundaries of basic geometric figures like squares and rectangles.

concepts.name: Perimeter
concepts.definition: Perimeter is the total distance around the boundary of a two-dimensional geometric shape.

concepts.name: Properties of Quadrilaterals
concepts.definition: Properties of quadrilaterals are the geometric attributes—such as side lengths, angles, and symmetry—that define and distinguish four-sided polygons.

concepts.name: Length Scale Factors in Similar Shapes
concepts.definition: Length scale factor is the constant ratio of corresponding linear dimensions between two similar geometric shapes.

concepts.name: Reflection
concepts.definition: Reflection is the metacognitive process of reviewing one's own thinking, problem-solving strategies, and learning experiences to improve future performance.

concepts.name: Rotation
concepts.definition: Rotation is a transformation that moves a shape around a fixed point, called the center of rotation, by a given angle.

concepts.name: Enlargement
concepts.definition: Enlargement is a geometric transformation that changes the size of a shape by a constant scale factor relative to a fixed point.

concepts.name: Translation and Vectors
concepts.definition: Translation and Vectors: The mathematical process of moving points or objects in a coordinate system using directed magnitude and direction.

concepts.name: Solving Linear Inequalities
concepts.definition: Solving linear inequalities is the process of finding the range of variable values that satisfy an inequality statement.

concepts.name: Linear Sequences (nth term)
concepts.definition: The rule defining a linear sequence, expressed as an algebraic formula (nth term) that calculates any term's value.

concepts.name: Compound Area
concepts.definition: Compound Area is the total space occupied by a shape formed from two or more simpler geometric figures.

concepts.name: Measuring Angles
concepts.definition: Measuring angles is the process of determining the size of the geometric angle formed by two intersecting lines or rays.

concepts.name: Basic Angle Facts (straight line, opposite, around a point, etc)
concepts.definition: Basic angle facts are fundamental geometric principles describing the relationships between angles formed by intersecting lines or points.

concepts.name: Angle Facts with Parallel Lines
concepts.definition: The set of geometric relationships between angles formed when a transversal intersects two parallel lines.

concepts.name: Angles in Polygons
concepts.definition: The sum of interior angles in a polygon is determined by the number of sides, calculated using a specific formula.

concepts.name: Parts of a Circle
concepts.definition: Parts of a circle are the distinct geometric components, including the radius, diameter, circumference, and center, that define its structure.

concepts.name: Volume of Prisms
concepts.definition: The amount of three-dimensional space occupied by a prism, calculated as the product of its base area and height.

concepts.name: Construct Angle
concepts.definition: The ability to accurately create a specific angle using tools like a protractor or compass.

concepts.name: Construct Triangle
concepts.definition: Construct Triangle: The ability to accurately draw a triangle given specific side lengths, angle measures, or a combination of both.

concepts.name: Construct Angle and Line Bisectors
concepts.definition: The ability to accurately draw a line or ray that divides a given angle or line segment into two equal parts.

concepts.name: Place Value
concepts.definition: Place value is the numerical system principle where a digit's value depends on its position within a number.

concepts.name: Mental Multiplication and Division
concepts.definition: Mental multiplication and division is the cognitive ability to perform arithmetic operations involving multiplication and division without external aids.

concepts.name: Written Multiplication
concepts.definition: Written multiplication is a computational method for finding the product of two numbers by sequentially multiplying digits and summing partial products.

concepts.name: Time
concepts.definition: Time is the duration a learner spends interacting with educational content or tasks.

concepts.name: Ordering Negative Numbers
concepts.definition: Ordering negative numbers is arranging integers less than zero from least to greatest based on their value on the number line.

concepts.name: Adding and Subtracting Negative Numbers
concepts.definition: Adding and subtracting negative numbers involves performing arithmetic operations on integers less than zero, following sign rules for combining values.

concepts.name: Multiplying and Dividing Negative Numbers
concepts.definition: Multiplying and dividing negative numbers involves applying sign rules to determine whether the product or quotient is positive or negative.

concepts.name: Factors and Highest Common Factor
concepts.definition: Factors are numbers that divide exactly into another number; the Highest Common Factor is the largest factor shared by two or more numbers.

concepts.name: Multiples and Lowest Common Multiple
concepts.definition: The smallest positive integer that is a multiple of two or more given numbers, representing their shared multiple.

concepts.name: Prime Numbers and Prime Factors
concepts.definition: Prime numbers are positive integers greater than one with exactly two distinct divisors. Prime factors are the prime numbers that multiply to form a given integer.

concepts.name: Multiplying and Dividing with Decimals
concepts.definition: The ability to accurately compute products and quotients involving decimal numbers, applying place value understanding and arithmetic operations.

concepts.name: Fractions of an Amount
concepts.definition: Fractions of an amount refers to calculating a proportional part of a given whole quantity using fractional multiplication.

concepts.name: Equivalent Fractions
concepts.definition: Equivalent fractions are different fractional representations that denote the same numerical value or proportion of a whole.

concepts.name: Ordering Fractions
concepts.definition: Ordering fractions is arranging a set of fractions in a sequence based on their relative numerical value, from least to greatest or vice versa.

concepts.name: Converting Mixed Number and Improper Fractions
concepts.definition: Converting a mixed number to an improper fraction involves multiplying the whole number by the denominator and adding the numerator.

concepts.name: Adding and Subtracting Fractions
concepts.definition: Adding and subtracting fractions involves combining or separating fractional parts, requiring a common denominator to ensure accurate numerical operations.

concepts.name: Multiplying Fractions
concepts.definition: Multiplying fractions is the arithmetic operation of finding the product of two or more fractions by multiplying their numerators and denominators.

concepts.name: Dividing Fractions
concepts.definition: Dividing fractions is the process of determining how many times one fractional quantity is contained within another.

concepts.name: Converting between Fractions and Decimals
concepts.definition: The ability to represent a rational number equivalently as a fraction or a decimal, and to perform the transformation between these two forms.

concepts.name: Converting between Fractions and Percentages
concepts.definition: Converting between fractions and percentages involves expressing a fractional value as an equivalent part per hundred, and vice versa.

concepts.name: Squares, Cubes, etc
concepts.definition: The concept of powers, where a number is multiplied by itself a specified number of times, such as squared or cubed.

concepts.name: Simplifying Expressions by Collecting Like Terms
concepts.definition: Simplifying expressions by collecting like terms is combining terms with identical variable parts to reduce an algebraic expression to its simplest form.

concepts.name: Horizontal and Vertical Lines
concepts.definition: Horizontal and vertical lines are straight lines that run parallel to the x-axis or y-axis, respectively, in a Cartesian coordinate system.

concepts.name: Length, Area and Volume Scale Factors
concepts.definition: Length, area, and volume scale factors describe the proportional change in corresponding linear, square, and cubic measurements when a shape is scaled.

concepts.name: Line Symmetry
concepts.definition: Line symmetry is a property where a shape can be divided into two identical halves that are mirror images of each other.

concepts.name: Rotational Symmetry
concepts.definition: Rotational symmetry is the property of a shape that appears identical after being rotated by less than a full turn around a central point.

concepts.name: Naming Co-ordinates in 2D
concepts.definition: The ability to correctly identify and label a point's location on a two-dimensional plane using an ordered pair (x, y).

concepts.name: Midpoint Between Two Co-ordinates
concepts.definition: The point on a line segment that divides it into two equal lengths, determined by averaging the x and y coordinates.

concepts.name: Gradient Between Two Co-ordinates
concepts.definition: The rate of change of a line connecting two points, calculated as the vertical difference divided by the horizontal difference.

concepts.name: Angles in Triangles
concepts.definition: The sum of interior angles in any triangle equals 180 degrees, a fundamental geometric property.

concepts.name: Missing Lengths
concepts.definition: Missing lengths are unknown numerical values in geometric figures that must be calculated using given measurements and mathematical relationships.
